    How Program, Study, Sub-study, Task and Milestone differ

    2026-10-27 · Fisheries Evaluation Studies, 23 rows · on the adopted defaults: medium rows, About folded below 1600px

    Today every row is drawn alike: a level word, then a name at one size. They aren't alike. Parents summarize their children; Tasks and Milestones are what you plan and move. Each treatment below is the running chart on the defaults adopted this morning.

    The rules

    1. Only Tasks and Milestones are things you move. They get the bar with depth and grips. Parents are flat summary brackets with no lift.
    2. Hierarchy by weight and indent, not words. The column header names the levels once.
    3. Weight steps down the tree. Program 650, Study 600, Sub-study 550 in grey, Task 450.
    4. A Milestone is a diamond at Task level, named like a task, no bar.
    5. Programs become sections (a band, rows beneath start fresh) once a plan has more than one.
    6. One row height for every level.
    7. Budget leaves the outline. It's in the hover readout and About; parents' totals step back to grey wherever they show. (Changed from this morning: see Width.)

    Today against the rules
